settings.description:
As your child grows, the chair they need keeps changing - which is why there is MOLTI. A floor seat that cradles the lower back for a first-ever chair, a high chair that shapes mealtime habits as solids begin, and a desk chair that holds good posture at the desk.

One baby chair that changes along with your child's growth - that is why MOLTI is called the multi-player.

settings.heading: MOLTI dimensions
settings.figures: Maximum load 40 kg. Product weight approximately 6.3 kg (floor seat), 7.9 kg (high chair), 8.5 kg (high chair with inner seat) or 6.3 kg (desk chair).
settings.caveats:
*Measurements may vary by plus or minus 20 mm and 1 kg depending on where and how they are taken; this is not a fault.
*Dimensions are measured with nobody seated.
*Seat height is measured at the centre of the seat.

settings.title: Tray on the desk chair: tipping risk
settings.body: With the desk-chair legs fitted, using the tray is not recommended - the combination risks tipping. Leave the tray and safety bar off in that configuration.

settings.title: Always fit a base before use
settings.body: For safe use the body must always be fitted with one of the bases: glides, the long legs or the desk-chair legs.

settings.title: Removing stains from the frame
settings.body: If the frame gets marked during assembly or use, a melamine sponge lifts stains easily. *Rubbing hard can damage the surface.
settings.alt: Cleaning the MOLTI frame

settings.question: What is the difference between the Hello Baby set and the High Chair set?
settings.answer: The Hello Baby set includes everything for all three configurations - floor seat, high chair and desk chair. The High Chair set omits the glides, inner seat and desk-chair legs (the inner seat and desk-chair legs are sold separately).

settings.question: Until when is the inner seat used?
settings.answer: The inner seat steadies babies from the time they hold their heads up while their lower backs are still weak - usually to around 12 months, though it varies with each child's development.

settings.question: The legs look mottled - is that a fault?
settings.answer: No - the grain pattern on the legs is a natural characteristic of the timber and is not grounds for exchange or return.
